text:
Anya L: Quick question — hitting a dims mismatch when using the rerank_batch helper + pagination. Embeddings are 1536 but our reranker code expects 1024. Any quick wins?
Sam K: which embedding model and which rerank helper are you using? :eyes:
Anya L: text-embedding-3-large for embeddings. Using the internal rerank_batch helper in sdk-js (the one that paginates and then calls rerank). Error shows:
```
ValueError: vector size mismatch: expected 1024, got 1536
at rerank_batch (/lib/rerank.js:42:15)
```
Anya L: repro: single batch of 120 docs, page_size=50, we concat pages and pass to reranker.
Devon: ah — two things to check quickly: model metadata (embedding dim) and whether the rerank helper is hard-coded to an older dim. We used 1024 internal for legacy model.
Devon: you can query model meta if you want: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/models/text-embedding-3-large` — look for `embedding_dimensions` in the JSON.
Maria P: also watch for partial page padding. If your concat logic drops an item or pads with zeros you'll get weird lengths. Quick pattern I use in TS:
```ts
async function* pages(items, pageSize){
  for(let i=0;i<items.length;i+=pageSize) yield items.slice(i,i+pageSize)
}
for await (const page of pages(docs,50)){
  const embs = await client.embeddings.create({ model, input: page });
  pushToBuffer(embs.data.map(e=>e.embedding));
}
// after loop: flatten buffer and pass to rerank
```
Maria P: ensure you don't accidentally flatten the outer array twice.
Ben R: another quick option: have rerank helper accept an explicit dim param or infer from first vector. E.g. `rerank({vectors, dim: vectors[0].length})` — small defensive fix.
Sam K: +1, inference on first vector is safe if you validate all vectors match that length before calling.
Anya L: good call. I quickly inspected model meta and it returns `embedding_dimensions: 1536`. So the helper is stale.
Devon: ok — two low-risk fixes: (1) update helper to infer dim and validate, (2) add clear error message suggesting model mismatch and include model name. I'll open a PR.
Anya L: re: pagination + rerank ordering — do we keep original indexes across pages? I want to preserve doc id ordering for downstream logging.
Devon: yes keep original doc id in the item object you pass through pages. E.g. attach `{id, text}` and map results back using id.
Maria P: streaming gotcha for rerank: if you use streaming embeddings (streaming tokens -> embeddings partials), the rerank endpoint expects the final vector. Don't feed partial streaming frames.
Anya L: noted. Also saw a streaming quirk: sdk-js streaming emitter emits 'data' chunks then final 'done' event; if code calls rerank on first 'data' it fails.
Ben R: add a small guard: `if (!chunk.done) return` before rerank.
CI Bot: nightly/embeds tests: embed-rerank-pager — failed on dim-assertion (flaky helper). Full log: https://ci.redwood.ai/abc/123 (truncated).
Anya L: I'll patch helper and add a unit that asserts all vectors same length and errors with helpful message incl detected model dims.
Sam K: also consider an opt-in `auto_cast` that will down-project or upsample? but that's risky. maybe suggest fallback_model param.
Devon: don't auto-resize silently. Add a helper util `ensure_dim(vectors, expected)` that throws or returns normalized float32 arrays only when explicit `allow_resize=true`.
Maria P: ping me for review, happy to check tests and pagination edge cases.
Anya L: thanks — I'll open PR and ping @Maria P and @Devon for review when done. :thumbsup:
